source.title: Minimum Moves to Balance Circular Array

teaching.hint: With only one deficit, how much does it cost to bring one unit from each other position?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Conservation decides feasibility; every unit supplied to the sole deficit costs at least its circular distance, and those costs can be attained independently.
solution_outline.approach: If the total balance is negative, report impossibility. Otherwise gather enough surplus units from increasing circular distances around the deficit, charging distance per unit; avoid counting the opposite position twice.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The remaining deficit is the number of units still needed; processed positions contain all sources closer than the current distance, and cost equals selected units’ distances.
solution_outline.correctness: Any feasible plan moves the needed units across at least their shortest circular distances. Selecting nearest available units minimizes that lower bound, and routing along a shortest arc attains it.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n)` time and `O(1)` auxiliary space; 64-bit arithmetic is needed for totals and move counts.
solution_outline.pitfall: On an even cycle, the position opposite the deficit appears in both outward directions and must be counted once.

common_wrong_turns: Use linear instead of wraparound distance
source_fidelity_notes: The at-most-one-negative guarantee is central and retained.
